caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Mozambique's debt is the product of Africa's most notorious hidden-debt scandal. From 31.2% of GDP in 2007 it climbed as the government secretly guaranteed over $2 billion in loans (2013-14) for tuna-fishing and maritime security companies; when revealed in 2016, donors and the IMF suspended support, the metical collapsed, and the ratio hit 124.8% in 2016, the series high. Mozambique missed a sovereign bond payment in early 2017, effectively defaulting. Restructuring and the 2022-23 start of LNG revenues brought it down, but it remains above 100%: 102.3% projected for 2025. The scandal's legacy is a debt stock that will take a generation of gas revenues to clear.
inflation_management: Mozambique's inflation tracks the metical and the debt saga. It ran at 10-14% in 2006-2011, then moderated to 2-6% in 2012-2015. The 2016 hidden-debt revelation crashed the currency and sent inflation to 18.4%, the series high, with 15.8% in 2017. Tighter policy and IMF re-engagement stabilized it: 0.9% in 2020, the series low. The 2022 global shock pushed it to 10.4%, easing to a projected 4.4% in 2025. The central bank has rebuilt credibility since 2016, but with debt over 100% of GDP and LNG revenues still ramping, monetary stability rests on a fragile fiscal foundation.

key_events.event: Government secretly guaranteed $2bn+ in loans (tuna bonds); debt began its surge.
Hidden debts revealed; IMF and donors suspended support; metical collapsed; inflation hit 18.4%.
Missed sovereign bond payment, entering default; debt hit 124.8% of GDP.
Cabo Delgado insurgency forced TotalEnergies to suspend its $20bn LNG project.
Coral South FLNG began producing; first LNG cargoes shipped, starting the gas era.
October 2024: Daniel Chapo won disputed elections amid fraud claims and deadly protests.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is gas-led growth with debt slowly declining from over 100% of GDP, but everything depends on LNG projects staying on track and the insurgency staying contained. Upside is transformational: Mozambique could become a major LNG exporter; downside is that the hidden-debt legacy, conflict, and political instability waste the windfall. Uncertainty is high: the economics are promising, the governance record is the worst in the region.
